name: Generate Blog Post

on:
  schedule:
    # Daily at 8:00 AM UTC. The duplicate/mis-title problems that once
    # justified a 3x/week cadence are now caught by the pipeline's hard
    # duplicate guard, H1 title reconciliation, and the CI content tests,
    # so daily drafting is safe again.
    - cron: '0 8 * * *'
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      mode:
        description: 'Generation mode'
        required: true
        default: 'auto'
        type: choice
        options:
          - auto
          - topic
          - git
      topic:
        description: 'Topic (required when mode is "topic")'
        required: false
        type: string

permissions:
  contents: write
  pull-requests: write

# Avoid two scheduled runs and a manual dispatch racing each other into
# duplicate PRs against `master`.
concurrency:
  group: blog-post-generator
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  generate:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
    steps:
      # Actions are pinned to full commit SHAs so a moved/compromised tag
      # can't inject code into a workflow that holds `contents: write`.
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0  # full history for git-log mode

      - uses: actions/setup-node@820762786026740c76f36085b0efc47a31fe5020 # v7.0.0
        with:
          node-version: 22

      - name: Generate blog post draft
        env:
          GEMINI_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.GEMINI_API_KEY }}
          GEMINI_MODEL: 'gemini-2.5-flash'
          INPUT_MODE: ${{ github.event.inputs.mode || 'auto' }}
          INPUT_TOPIC: ${{ github.event.inputs.topic || '' }}
        run: |
          case "$INPUT_MODE" in
            auto|topic|git) ;;
            *) echo "Invalid mode: $INPUT_MODE" >&2; exit 1 ;;
          esac

          if [ "$INPUT_MODE" = "topic" ] && [ -n "$INPUT_TOPIC" ]; then
            node scripts/generate-post-gemini.js topic "$INPUT_TOPIC"
          else
            node scripts/generate-post-gemini.js "$INPUT_MODE"
          fi

      - name: Check for new draft
        id: check
        run: |
          if git status --porcelain | grep -q 'blog-src/src/content/posts/'; then
            DRAFT_FILE=$(git status --porcelain | grep 'blog-src/src/content/posts/' | awk '{print $2}' | head -1)
            # Title is AI-generated; never interpolate it directly into a shell command.
            # Sanitize aggressively (printable ASCII minus shell metacharacters) and cap length.
            RAW_TITLE=$(head -5 "$DRAFT_FILE" | grep '^title:' | sed 's/^title: *"//;s/"$//')
            SAFE_TITLE=$(printf '%s' "$RAW_TITLE" | tr -cd 'A-Za-z0-9 _.,:!?-' | head -c 120)
            {
              echo "has_draft=true"
              echo "draft_file=$DRAFT_FILE"
              echo "title=$SAFE_TITLE"
            } >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          else
            echo "has_draft=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "No new draft was generated."
          fi

      - name: Create PR with draft
        if: steps.check.outputs.has_draft == 'true'
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          DRAFT_TITLE: ${{ steps.check.outputs.title }}
          DRAFT_FILE: ${{ steps.check.outputs.draft_file }}
        run: |
          DATE=$(date +%Y-%m-%d)
          SLUG=$(printf '%s' "$DRAFT_TITLE" | tr '[:upper:]' '[:lower:]' | tr -cs 'a-z0-9' '-' | head -c 40)
          BRANCH="blog/draft-${DATE}-${SLUG}"

          git config user.name "github-actions[bot]"
          git config user.email "github-actions[bot]@users.noreply.github.com"

          git checkout -b "$BRANCH"
          git add blog-src/src/content/posts/
          git commit -m "draft: $DRAFT_TITLE"
          git push -u origin "$BRANCH"

          gh label create blog-draft --color "0E8A16" --description "Auto-generated blog draft" 2>/dev/null || true

          PR_BODY=$(cat <<EOF
          ## Auto-Generated Blog Draft

          **File:** \`${DRAFT_FILE}\`

          This post was automatically generated by the daily blog pipeline using Google Gemini.

          ### To publish:
          1. Review and edit the post in \`${DRAFT_FILE}\`
          2. Add appropriate tags in the frontmatter
          3. Merge this PR

          > **Note:** The post is written directly into \`posts/\`, so merging this PR
          > publishes and deploys it to the site. Close the PR without merging to discard.

          *Generated via GitHub Actions*
          EOF
          )

          gh pr create \
            --title "📝 Blog Draft: $DRAFT_TITLE" \
            --body "$PR_BODY" \
            --label "blog-draft" \
            --base master

I've made the code fixes, but I still need your help with one thing before I change any model names.

**Why the run failed** (scheduled run 35346314572, today):
1. `gemini-2.5-flash` returned 503 (overloaded) three times, so the script moved on to the next model in its fallback list.
2. That fallback, `gemini-2.0-flash`, has been retired. Google now returns a 404: *"This model models/gemini-2.0-flash is no longer available. Please update your code to use models/gemini-3.6-flash."*
3. **This is the actual bug:** `scripts/generate-post-gemini.js` stops the whole run on any error it doesn't retry, and a 404 is one of those. So the third model, `gemini-2.5-flash-lite`, was never tried.
4. Separately, the embedding model `text-embedding-004` also 404s now. That doesn't cause the failure, but duplicate detection has quietly fallen back to simple word-overlap matching instead of meaning-based similarity.

**Fixed so far (not committed):**
- **`scripts/generate-post-gemini.js`:** a 400 or 404 now skips to the next model instead of stopping the run. Bad-key errors (401/403) still stop immediately. One retired model name can no longer kill the pipeline.
- **`scripts/lib/blog-post.js`:** the embedding cache now includes the model name in its key. Without this, switching embedding models would compare vectors of different sizes and quietly give wrong duplicate scores in a local cache. CI starts with an empty cache, so it wasn't affected there. I added a regression test in `tests/lib/blog-post.test.js`; that file passes (61/61). The other two test files under `tests/lib` fail with or without my changes because the `blog-src` dependencies aren't installed here.

**What I need from you:** the Gemini API key isn't available on this machine, so I can't check which model names are valid now. The error message names `gemini-3.6-flash` but says nothing about the embedding model, and I don't want to guess. Could you run this where `GEMINI_API_KEY` is set:

```

```

With that list I'll:
- update the fallback chain in the script;
- update the embedding model default;
- update the pinned `GEMINI_MODEL` in `.github/workflows/generate-blog-post.yml`, which overrides the script's default in CI;
- check whether the `thinkingBudget: 0` setting still works on newer models. The topic picker only allows 100 output tokens, so a model that spends tokens "thinking" could return nothing.
- update the README and skill docs to match.

To confirm it really works, I'd then like to trigger the workflow once by hand in `topic` mode. Is that OK? A successful run pushes a branch and opens a real draft PR.

**Why it failed:** `gemini-2.5-flash` was temporarily overloaded (503), so the script tried its first fallback, `gemini-2.0-flash`. Google has retired that model and now returns a 404. The script treated the 404 as fatal and exited without trying its last fallback.

The embedding cache now includes the model name in its keys, so vectors from different models can't be compared by mistake. There's a new test for this; `tests/lib/blog-post.test.js` passes (61/61) and lint is clean.
- **Workflow:** the job timeout is now 20 minutes instead of 10. The failed run spent over 4 minutes retrying a single model, so a three-model chain could run past 10.
